knowledge_graph.title: GitHub
knowledge_graph.description: GitHub is a proprietary developer platform that allows developers to create, store, manage, and share their code. It uses Git to provide distributed version control, and GitHub itself provides access control, bug tracking, software feature requests, task management, continuous integration, and wikis for every project.

related_questions.question: Is GitHub free or paid?
related_questions.snippet: GitHub offers free and paid plans for storing and collaborating on code. Some plans are available only to personal accounts, while other plans are available only to organization and enterprise accounts.

related_questions.question: What is GitHub known for?
related_questions.snippet: GitHub is a platform for building software. Whether you are starting a new project or contributing to an existing one, GitHub brings together the tools and workflows you need across every stage of the software development life cycle (SDLC).
related_questions.title: What is GitHub? - GitHub Docs

related_questions.question: What is the main purpose of Git?
related_questions.snippet: Git is a version control system, a tool used to record and manage changes to files over time, especially in software development. A few things to know: Git allows multiple contributors to work on the same project, track edits, and maintain a full history of changes.
